function.name: get_law_categories
function.description: Retrieves the list of categories within a specified type of law. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

message.content:
**Yes – you can file a noise complaint in Atlanta.** In the United States, noise complaints are generally handled by the city’s **Code Enforcement** office or the **Police Department**, rather than by a “city council” in the way some other countries organize their local governments. Below are the most common ways to report a noise problem in Atlanta: | How to File | Contact Details | What to Include | |-------------|-----------------|-----------------| | **Online (311 Portal)** | | • Select “Noise” from the list of services.
• Fill out the form with the address, time(s) of disturbance, description of the source, and any supporting photos or audio clips.
• Submit. | | **Phone (311 Service Line)** | 404‑292‑4000 (for non‑emergency calls) | • Call during business hours (8 a.m.–5 p.m., Monday–Friday).
• Tell the operator you’re reporting a noise violation; they’ll route you to the appropriate department. | | **Direct to Code Enforcement** | 404‑292‑4000 (same as 311) or email: `code.enforcement@atlantaga.gov` | • Address: 100 Peachtree St. NE, Atlanta, GA 30303.
• Provide the same details as above. | | **Direct to Police (if urgent or ongoing)** | 404‑292‑4000 (or 911 for emergencies) | • If the noise is a crime (e.g., assault, vandalism), call 911 immediately. For non‑emergencies, call 404‑292‑4000 and ask to speak with the “Noise Complaint” unit. | ### What the City Looks For Atlanta’s Municipal Code (Title 10, Chapter 1, § 10‑1‑2) sets limits on allowable sound levels and defines “quiet hours.” Typical restrictions include: * **Quiet Hours:** 11 p.m.–7 a.m. on weekdays, 12 a.m.–7 a.m. on weekends. * **Allowed Decibel Levels:** Generally ≤ 55 dB during quiet hours, ≤ 70 dB during daytime (though this can vary by neighborhood). * **Prohibited Activities:** Loud music, amplified speech, construction noise, fireworks, etc., during restricted times. When filing, try to note: * Exact dates & times of the disturbance. * Location (street address or intersection). * Type of noise (music, construction, barking dogs, etc.). * Any witnesses or evidence (photos, videos, audio recordings). ### After You File * **Acknowledgment:** You’ll receive a confirmation number and a timeline for when the city will investigate. * **Investigation:** A Code Enforcement officer or police dispatcher will visit the site, measure decibel levels if necessary, and interview witnesses. * **Outcome:** If a violation is found, the offender may receive a warning, citation, or fine. Repeated violations can lead to higher penalties. --- #### Quick Tips 1. **File Early:** Report the first time you notice a violation—later reports may be harder to verify. 2. **Document Evidence:** Even a simple voice recording can help prove the noise level. 3. **Follow Up:** If you haven’t heard back within a week, call 404‑292‑4000 and reference your confirmation number. If you’re unsure whether your situation falls under a municipal noise ordinance (e.g., a neighbor’s party vs. a construction crew), you can always start by calling 404‑292‑4000 and asking the dispatcher for guidance. Good luck!
